thread:
Maya: FYI — proposal for a lightweight 'oncall scribe' we can pilot next week. idea: bot that joins the incident channel when severity>=2, transcribes the live chat (and optional voice bridge notes), extracts candidate action items, and auto-creates PM tickets + postmortem skeleton. want quick sanity check before i write the RFC.

Chen: love this. couple Qs: 1) who owns the action creation? bot should assign a placeholder owner or leave unassigned? 2) privacy: we must scrub customer PII automatically.

Liam: +1. For (1) my vote is: create tasks with suggested owners based on oncall rotation metadata, but let humans confirm. reduces friction but avoids bad auto-ownership.

Maya: agreed on suggested owners. thinking flow = bot joins -> records -> detects "action:" patterns or sentences like "need to follow up with X" -> propose items in channel as ephemeral blocks -> oncall confirms -> bot creates tickets in our tracker with postmortem template link.

Ravi: snooping on the NLP side: we can use simple regex + small classifier to reduce false positives. also rate-limit to avoid noise during SEV-1.

Emily: we should include a one-click "schedule postmortem" button in the action creation step that picks the calendar based on rotation and creates a meeting stub with the postmortem template attached. :calendar:

SRE-Bot: INCIDENT 2113456123 created by maya via /incident create — severity: 2 — region: us-east-1. Auto-join: eng-oncall, eng-sre, product-notify.

Maya: sample slash commands i'm thinking:
```
/scribe start 2113456123 --mode=transcribe --actions=detect --assign=suggest
/scribe stop 2113456123 --publish=ephemeral
/scribe publish 2113456123 --to=tracker --template=postmortem-v2
```
Give example UI for ephemeral prompt: bot lists 3 candidate actions with checkboxes + suggested owner + ETA fields.

Chen: we'll need a clear opt-out: sometimes infra teams don't want every debug log captured in tracker. add channel flag `#incidents-no-scribe` or conversation-level opt-out.

Liam: also add a customer-impact capture step — bot prompts: "Was customer-visible outage?" with quick options (no, degraded, full outage) and freeform field for customer IDs. Make that input scrubbed before ticket creation.

Maya: yes — propose capture fields: impact_level, affected_customers_list, estimated_duration, mitigation_summary, immediate_owner. Bot stores raw notes in ephemeral vault accessible only to incident lead for 7 days by default (audit logs).

Ravi: ops: how about action item format for tracker creation? simple JSON payload we can send to the tracker API:
```
{
  "title": "[INC-2113456123] Follow up: investigate cache eviction at t+5m",
  "description": "Auto-extracted from incident channel. Confidence: 0.82. Snippet: 'cache eviction spiked after deploy'",
  "labels": ["postincident", "scribe-auto"],
  "owner_suggested": "oncall-liam",
  "due": "2026-03-22"
}
```
Make sure we strip any customer emails.

SRE-Bot: Note: action creation API requires approver header. propose bot creates draft tasks and posts ephemeral summary for the incident lead. Only on confirming reaction :white_check_mark: does bot push to tracker with approver header.

Emily: good — reduces accidental noise. Also we should auto-tag items with severity & service/component. allows dashboard filtering.

Chen: what about handoffs? can bot attach a short handoff checklist when someone pings the rotation channel: e.g., `@oncall handoff` => bot posts prefilled form: current incidents, unresolved actions, suggested next steps.

Maya: yep. idea: `@scribe handoff` will snapshot open incidents + auto-generate a 3-bullet summary for the incoming oncall and attach links to draft actions. That snapshot is kept in the incident thread and in the rotation chat for traceability.

Liam: UX thought — during noisy incidents, avoid spamming the channel with bot messages. ephemeral prints only to the active responders; public message only when lead confirms.

Ravi: ops constraints: bot needs RBAC for ticket creation and view. ensure it respects confidential incident tagging and doesn't push to public trackers for customer-sensitive incidents. maybe postmortem creation requires an additional approval step from security for flagged incidents.

Maya: agreed. add a "sensitivity_level" field that flows into creation logic. default low, can be escalated by lead.

Chen: pilot plan? propose: 2-week sandbox in a duplicate channel (#incidents-sandbox) with synthetic incidents and one real minor incident shadowing. gather metrics: # actions auto-detected, confirmation rate, false positives, time saved scheduling PMs.

Emily: also measure customer-impact capture accuracy vs manual annotation. we'll need to compare 20 incidents annotated by humans vs bot extraction.

Maya: ok i'll draft a short RFC and checklist. immediate action items from this thread: 1) Maya to write RFC + design doc (owner: Maya) 2) Ravi to prototype NLP extraction model and heuristics (owner: Ravi) 3) Chen to scope RBAC + opt-out flags (owner: Chen) 4) Liam to design ephemeral UI + slash command UX (owner: Liam) 5) Emily to wire calendar & meeting stub flow (owner: Emily)

Liam: timeline suggestion: 1 week for RFC and infra sketch, 2 weeks for prototype, then 1 week sandbox test. total ~4 weeks.

SRE-Bot: Action created: "Draft RFC for oncall-scribe" assigned to Maya (due 2026-03-18) — link: https://tracker/redwood/INC-DRFT-1001

Maya: cool — scheduling kickoff sync Friday 10:30am. @everyone please react :thumbsup: if you can make it or :wave: if you can only async.

Ravi: :thumbsup:
